question: Should OpenClaw permit `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` on non-loopback or private-ingress Gateway binds, and if so what explicit guardrail or acknowledgement is required?
rationale: The requested behavior moves protection for reachable Gateway operator surfaces from OpenClaw auth to external infrastructure, which is a security-boundary and product-policy choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Boundary
options.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and treat trusted-proxy as the supported delegated-auth path.

options.title: Sponsor Guarded Private-Ingress Mode
options.body: Allow reachable no-auth only behind a deliberately named high-risk policy with startup warnings, audit findings, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Reject Core No-Auth Expansion
options.body: Close this direction as not planned after documenting why OpenClaw core will not support unauthenticated reachable Gateway binds.

recommendation.title: Keep Fail-Closed Boundary
recommendation.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and treat trusted-proxy as the supported delegated-auth path.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing candidate from recent Gateway auth hardening and security-boundary history.
